title: Configure and Troubleshoot SAML, LDAP, and RBAC
objectives: Configure and Troubleshoot SAML, LDAP, and RBAC
Verify actual permissions and active source with independent evidence.

tasks.instruction: Open Recorded security operations → Identity and role mapping on sh01. The fixture retains a failed SAML group mapping. Inspect native authentication.conf, the supplied teaching IdP metadata certificate and authorize.conf. Repair roleMap_samlv2 user=SocReaders and make the user role a reader of ops_logs with no indexes_edit, edit_roles or edit_monitor capabilities. Restart virtual sh01, review the active source, then probe the fictional SAML reader. Require roles=[user] and visibility of three actual ops_logs records.

Next configure one LDAP strategy named practice_ldap: directory.practice.invalid port 636, SSLEnabled=1, bindDN=cn=svc-splunk,ou=svc,dc=practice,dc=invalid, bindDNpassword=training-only. Use userBaseDN=ou=People,dc=practice,dc=invalid, groupBaseDN=ou=Groups,dc=practice,dc=invalid, userNameAttribute=uid, groupNameAttribute=cn, groupMappingAttribute=dn and groupMemberAttribute=member. Map user=SocReaders in roleMap_practice_ldap. Activate it, probe the LDAP reader, and retain both methods’ successful receipts plus the initial failure. These are explicit offline assertions/directory entries, not a real IdP, LDAP bind, cryptographic certificate or browser login.

In Search choose sh01 and practice principal analyst. Run index=ops_logs | stats count and inspect the job: expect count=3. Verify that index-editing permissions and protected indexes remain denied. Changing native source after a probe invalidates its current-source proof; review and probe again.

hints: Inspect running source and actual receipts before changing configuration.
Use the paused fixture clock deliberately; verify results through a separate view or query.
